# File and function comments

Anytime you touch a hand-written file in the lists below, **review** its header and the comments next to the change: refresh a stale description / Used by / Uses, add a why-comment if this edit introduced an odd bit, drop comments the code no longer matches. Do not restyle comments that are still true (including older headers that lack overflow notes).

Bring the **whole file** up to this standard on create or a meaningful rewrite of that file. Do not sweep untouched files.

**Do** — hand-written source (`src/**`), schema and seed files, framework config with logic in it, `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `infra/**`, `scripts/**`, `.githooks/*`.

**Skip** — generated code (ORM clients, `*-env.d.ts`, migrations SQL), lockfiles, dependencies, JSON configs (`package.json`, compiler configs), thin tool configs (eslint, postcss, test runner), and prose docs (`docs/`, README, `AGENTS.md`, `.cursor/rules`).

Write like a staff engineer briefing a junior: skim bullets, what + why, no essays.

## File header

The header is the scan surface: someone grasping the architecture reads only these lines, so **every one of them is a single line**. Anything longer goes in a paragraph below — it never widens a labeled line.

First line is the description (what this file is) with no `What:` label. Then:

- **In the app** — how it fits (who cares, when it runs)
- **Used by** — callers (names/paths, not a paragraph)
- **Uses** — important deps (skip React/Tailwind noise); omit the line if nothing non-obvious

Add **Watch** only if the *whole file* exists for an edge, security, or "looks unused" reason — still one line.

One line each is a hard limit. If context will not fit (pipeline, install steps, onboarding explanation, edge case, a threat that needs two sentences), keep the labeled lines short and add it as a paragraph **after a blank line**. Same comment syntax, prose there, not an essay. Do not stuff overflow into the description / In the app / Used by / Uses / Watch. The single-line rule is for skimmability, not for cutting content: never compress real information out of a header line just to keep it to one line — push it to the paragraph instead.

TypeScript / JS — plain `/* … */` block at the top, no `*` gutter on the inner lines, just open and close (immediately after `"use client"` / `"use server"` if present; imports below):

```ts
/*
  Note CRUD against Postgres for one user.
  In the app: the only write path for notes; API handlers call this, never the UI.
  Used by: the notes API handlers; archive also triggers the search reindex.
  Uses: the notes repository port, mapNote, reindexUserNotes.

  Archive leaves rows so links and history still resolve; the UI hides archived notes.
*/
```

Schema files, Terraform, Dockerfile, YAML, shell — same labeled lines with that language's comment syntax (`//` or `#`). Dockerfile: keep `# syntax=` as line 1; header goes on line 2. Examples: `docs-infra.mdc`.

## Function notes

One `//` line directly above the function is preferred: what it does, plus where it matters if the header doesn't already say. No JSDoc `@param` / `@returns`. Do not restate the identifier (`// Creates a note` is banned).

```ts
// Loads this user's notes; the notes list and the dashboard start here.
export const listNotes = async (...) => { ... }

// YYYY-MM-DD for storage/API; never a Date object past this helper.
export const toDateKey = (date: Date | string): string => { ... }
```

If one line isn't enough — a non-obvious algorithm, a gotcha for callers, a why that needs more than a clause — keep that first line as the single-line summary and add a paragraph underneath (blank line, then prose, same `//` syntax). The single-line rule is for skimmability, not for cutting content: never compress real information out of the comment just to keep it to one line.

```ts
// Reconciles local queue against server state; runs on reconnect.
//
// Server is source of truth for ordering, but locally-queued writes made
// while offline must replay after the reconcile or they're silently dropped.
export const reconcileQueue = async (...) => { ... }
```

Skip obvious one-line getters. Tests: same file header; only comment helpers/setup that `it("...")` doesn't already say. If a test exists only to lock an edge/security case, one line why.

## Scripts — `scripts/*`, `.githooks/*`

Narrated line by line, not why-only: `docs-scripts.mdc` (loads when you open one).

## Why comments (required)

Comment on the line above the odd bit — **what + why**. Use whenever a junior would want to "clean it up":

- **Weird / uncommon / edge** — what edge, what breaks without it
- **Security** — the threat and the cost of dropping it
- **Looks unnecessary but required** — why it looks dead and why it isn't (hydration, localhost vs prod, eslint-disable with a real reason)

```ts
// Forces HTTP → HTTPS. Fine on the real hosts; breaks `pnpm dev` on http://localhost.
...(secureTransport ? ["upgrade-insecure-requests"] : [])

// Keep one DOM shape for SSR + first client paint so next-themes cannot skew hydration.
const activeId = mounted && isThemeId(theme) ? theme : "dark";
```

Bad: `// security` / `# edge case` / `// don't remove` with no why.

When rewriting existing comments, convert to this format — don't stack a second style. Keep real constraints (eslint-disable, hydration, security); tighten vague ones to what + why.
